summary: Dorchester County, MD tower built 1932, decommissioned about 1978 and dismantled in 2018; its top 40 feet was restored at the DNR Church Creek field office, open to the public but not for climbing.

facts.design: 120-foot steel tower (1932 notice); Aermotor tower with 7 by 7 foot metal cab and rooftop catwalk (NHLR); restored top 40 feet kept
facts.agency: Maryland DNR Forest Service (NHLR); DNR Church Creek Forestry Field Office (ACEC)

access.note: Small park with interpretive panels and an accessible parking area; a Maryland Historic Trust agreement required the tower be opened to the public (ACEC). The register says the restored tower is not open for climbing.

visit.trail_note: Tower is less than 200 feet off Golden Hill Road, with ADA accessible parking (ACEC)

events.note: Constructed by the Maryland Forest Service as a 120-foot tower; 1932 notice gives a site 4 feet above sea level
Decommissioned circa 1978 as fire detection technology advanced, then stood idle for about 40 years (ACEC)
Dismantled in 2018 for deteriorating and unsafe conditions; DNR kept the top 40 feet, including the cab, for restoration

Restored top 40 feet renovated as an educational display at the DNR Church Creek Forestry Field Office; the register says work was complete as of 2024. The ACEC project ran from Nov 1, 2022 to Oct 31, 2024

corrections.why: The record's point (NHLR) is about 16 km north of the point Firelookout.org gives for the original Church Creek tower. The 2007 DNR report places the tower 2.2 miles south of the town of Church Creek, which fits the Firelookout.org point better. The proposed point is the index entry and has not been checked against a map; a human should verify it before applying.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR describes the tower as at the Church Creek Forestry station and 'used in emergencies'; the ACEC account says it was decommissioned around 1978, stood idle, and was dismantled in 2018. The story follows the ACEC timeline and notes the NHLR wording.
NHLR's description says both 100' and 120' Aermotor tower; the 1932 notice and ACEC give 120 feet. The restored structure is the top 40 feet (12.2 m), which is the facts.height_m value.

notes_for_editor: Dates 1932, 2018 and 2024 agree across NHLR and ACEC. Unresolved: (1) Status 'relocated' may overstate the move. ACEC says the top 40 feet was dismantled in 2018 and erected at the DNR field office, but the 2007 DNR report and NHLR place the original at or near the Church Creek Forestry station. The sources do not say whether the restored tower stands far from the original. (2) Location: the record's NHLR point (38.62328, -76.13468) is far from both the DNR 2007 description and the Firelookout.org entries (38.47420). See corrections; a human should check against a map. (3) The index lists NHLR US 696 only on the original entry, not on the display entry, which is why the brief's 'shared register number' note is only partly borne out. (4) The ACEC entry is a contractor's award submission, so its dates are treated as the owner's account. Budget: 1 WebSearch and about 6 page reads, within limits.
